title: archive: map v3 file capability rootid to the container namespace
body:
A v3 "security.capability" xattr embeds a rootid identifying the UID that owns the capability. When the diff of an id-shifted layer is archived, file ownership is remapped from host IDs back to container IDs, but the rootid of the capability was left as a host-specific UID (e.g. 1000000, the first host ID of the mapping). Such a value is meaningless to other consumers of the layer and makes the kernel return EOVERFLOW when the capability is later read back through an id-mapped mount.

Remap the rootid host->container when writing the diff, downgrading the value to v2 when it maps to container root.

Closes: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-160859

@jnovy PTAL

For 1.62 (podman 5.8) we also need to partially backport 599dbf62fc:

```diff
diff --git a/storage/layers.go b/storage/layers.go
index d485c9b4fa..ddf7b1edfb 100644
--- a/storage/layers.go
+++ b/storage/layers.go
@@ -1575,6 +1575,13 @@ func (r *layerStore) create(id string, parentLayer *Layer, names []string, mount
 	}
 
 	idMappings := idtools.NewIDMappingsFromMaps(moreOptions.UIDMap, moreOptions.GIDMap)
+	if moreOptions.HostUIDMapping && moreOptions.HostGIDMapping {
+		// The layer is host-mapped: its content stays at identity ownership and
+		// any id shifting happens at mount time. Rechowning to the container's
+		// maps here would double-shift the content once the id-mapped mount is
+		// applied, so keep the rechown target at identity.
+		idMappings = &idtools.IDMappings{}
+	}
 	opts := drivers.CreateOpts{
 		MountLabel: mountLabel,
 		StorageOpt: options,
diff --git a/storage/store.go b/storage/store.go
index 3d8ea50759..3f08867e9c 100644
--- a/storage/store.go
+++ b/storage/store.go
@@ -1986,20 +1986,17 @@ func (s *store) CreateContainer(id string, names []string, image, layer, metadat
 		// But in transient store mode, all container layers are volatile.
 		Volatile: options.Volatile || s.transientStore,
 	}
-	if s.canUseShifting(uidMap, gidMap) {
-		layerOptions.IDMappingOptions = types.IDMappingOptions{
-			HostUIDMapping: true,
-			HostGIDMapping: true,
-			UIDMap:         nil,
-			GIDMap:         nil,
-		}
-	} else {
-		layerOptions.IDMappingOptions = types.IDMappingOptions{
-			HostUIDMapping: idMappingsOptions.HostUIDMapping,
-			HostGIDMapping: idMappingsOptions.HostGIDMapping,
-			UIDMap:         copySlicePreferringNil(uidMap),
-			GIDMap:         copySlicePreferringNil(gidMap),
-		}
+	// When the driver supports shifting, the layer content is left at its
+	// identity ownership and the mapping is applied at mount time. Record the
+	// caller's maps but flag the layer as host-mapped so create() does not
+	// physically rechown the content into the container's range (which would
+	// then be shifted a second time by the id-mapped mount).
+	useHostMapping := idMappingsOptions.HostUIDMapping || s.canUseShifting(uidMap, gidMap)
+	layerOptions.IDMappingOptions = types.IDMappingOptions{
+		HostUIDMapping: useHostMapping,
+		HostGIDMapping: useHostMapping,
+		UIDMap:         copySlicePreferringNil(uidMap),
+		GIDMap:         copySlicePreferringNil(gidMap),
 	}
 	if options.Flags == nil {
 		options.Flags = make(map[string]any)
```

comments.body:
> Can we explicitly write down why this mapping only needs to happen when creating archives, and not extracting them?
> 
> [torvalds/linux@f2b00be](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/f2b00be488730522d0fb7a8a5de663febdcefe0a) suggests that if we convert a namespaced-v3 xattr into a v2 one on layer push, and write a v2 one on layer pull, then using the xattr from inside the container will fail (the host-UID 0 will not be mapped into the container).

OK:

- In our ordinary operation, (after this PR); the capability value, as visible from both the host (possibly from Podman’s rootless namespace) and the container, is a v2 one.

On reflection, that makes sense: we _create_ archives from a container (possibly with a non-default namespace, so we need to map) but _extract_ them as images (without https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/28393 , always host-mapped). So, we extract a v2 xattr (when rootless, the kernel will physically create a v3 one), and we (possibly through 2 sets of mappings, host -> container IDs and container IDs -> container namespace) see “the right root” inside the container.

---

I thought it _would_ be an issue with https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/28393 / https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/717 , if we don’t use shifting… I see, after a rootless `podman run --uidmap=`:
- The pull creates files that reflect (<s>well…to be discussed elsewhere</s>) the ID map
- `security.capability` is v3 ID with root = my rootless on-host user (what I’d expect without any explicit conversion step, when creating a v2 value inside the basic Podman’s rootless user namespace), _but does not reflect `--uidmap`_
- Nevertheless, from inside the running container, it’s a valid v2 ID and it actually works to grant capabilities.

What I missed is https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/89a312991dc6e638a36adc43ccb91dbc25504c04/security/commoncap.c#L494 : When using a v3 ID, even if the the v3 ID root does not map into the current namespace at all, as long as it is a root in _any parent_ namespace, it is treated as a valid root, and the value is treated as a valid v2 ID.

So this all works fine.

> LGTM, is there a e2e test case we could add to buildah based on the given reproducer? Would be nice to ensure this works where we need it to and not just as part of the unit tests here

@Luap99 test added here: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/pull/7086
